system:
You are a document classifier. Classification errors propagate to
extraction, routing and downstream processing, so accuracy and an honest
account of your reasoning are both required.

CATEGORIES:
- indications_and_usage: the conditions the drug is approved to treat
- dosage_and_administration: how much to give, how often, and by what route
- contraindications: situations in which the drug must not be used at all
- adverse_reactions: side effects and reactions observed in patients
- drug_interactions: effects of taking this drug alongside other drugs or foods
- overdosage: signs of overdose and how to manage one
- how_supplied: dosage forms, strengths, packaging and storage
- description: chemical name, structure, formulation and inactive ingredients
- pediatric_use: what is known about use in children
- geriatric_use: what is known about use in patients 65 and older

BEFORE STATING YOUR CLASSIFICATION:
1. List the 3 most prominent features of this document that inform
   classification.
2. Name the 2 categories that are most plausible, and why each is.
3. State which one wins, and what specifically ruled the other out.

OUTPUT FORMAT (strict JSON):
{
  "reasoning": "<your step-by-step analysis>",
  "classification": "<CATEGORY>",
  "runner_up": "<the second most likely category>",
  "ruled_out_because": "<what decided it against the runner-up>"
}

If the evidence genuinely does not separate the top two, say so in
"ruled_out_because" and put the weaker one in "runner_up" anyway. Do not
manufacture a distinction that is not in the document.
user:
<passage>
Furosemide Tablets, USP 80 mg: White-off white, round, scored, debossed "3171" over "V" on one side and plain on the reverse side, available as follows: • Bottles of 500: NDC 63629-1120-1 You may report side effects to Solco Healthcare US, LLC at 1-866-257-2597 or FDA at 1-800-FDA-1088 or www.fda.gov/medwatch . STORAGE Store at 20° to 25°C (68° to 77°F) [see USP Controlled Room Temperature]. Protect from light. Dispense in well-closed, light-resistant containers. Exposure to light might cause a slight discoloration. Discolored tablets should not be dispensed.
</passage>
response: {"reasoning": "1. Most prominent features: (a) This passage specifies physical tablet characteristics (80 mg strength, white-off white, round, scored, debossed markings); (b) NDC number and packaging information (bottles of 500); (c) Storage instructions (20-25°C, protect from light, light-resistant containers). 2. Two most plausible categories: (a) 'how_supplied' - The document explicitly describes dosage form (tablets), strength (80 mg), appearance details (color, shape, scoring, imprinting), packaging quantity (bottles of 500), and includes NDC number, all hallmark elements of how_supplied sections. (b) 'description' - The passage does provide descriptive information about the tablet's physical characteristics and formulation presentation. However, description sections typically emphasize chemical composition, chemical name, inactive ingredients, and formulation science, whereas this passage focuses on the commercial/physical presentation aspects. 3. The winner is 'how_supplied' because: The passage directly addresses supply and distribution details (NDC, packaging bottles of 500), storage conditions (which are part of how_supplied), and the specific physical identifiers needed for product identification in pharmacy settings. The storage instruction is placed here because it relates to how the product is supplied and maintained. The 'description' category is ruled out because there is no mention of chemical name, inactive ingredients, chemical structure, or formulation composition - only the tablet appearance and packaging information.", "classification": "how_supplied", "runner_up": "description", "ruled_out_because": "The passage lacks any discussion of chemical composition, inactive ingredients, chemical name, or formulation science that would characterize a description section. It focuses entirely on commercial presentation, packaging, NDC coding, and storage—all elements of how_supplied rather than the scientific/compositional description of the drug itself."}
